newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: RUGBY UNION-TIREDNESS A MAJOR CONCERN FOR HART.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-TIREDNESS A MAJOR CONCERN FOR HART.

text.p: AUCKLAND, Aug 11 - Last season's lessons from Ellis Park will be revised carefully by the All Black rugby team management this week when they attempt to pump up the team for the eighth time in 10 weeks, NZPA reports.
Players looked ragged and drained as they nursed cuts, bruises and bumps yesterday following Saturday's 55-35 Tri-Series test win against the Springboks at Eden Park.

All Black coach John Hart was concerned with their tiredness, saying his test players were physically and mentally drained and it would take a major effort to lift them for Saturday's clash with the freshened Wallabies at Carisbrook.
With eight tests in 10 weeks combined with travel to and from South Africa, it was taking longer for players to recover, he said.

Yesterday's team resembled the 1996 Ellis Park test side in terms of their physical state. It was their last game as well in a similar programme to this year's and followed three tests against South Africa on consecutive weekends.
As it transpired, that test was their only loss of the past season.
"We don't want to make the same mistake as we did at Ellis Park last year," Hart said.

For that reason Hart has named only his squad, the same as last week's, and added Jon Preston to the side to give him more selection flexibility for the bench, with the use of substitutions in mind at this stage.
He will name the test team on Wednesday after assessing their physical state. The squad assembles in Dunedin on Tuesday.
Hart said none of his players carried serious injuries and all should be available for selection.
The Australians, who had a bye last weekend, arrive in the country on Wednesday.
